title: Sam Altman sympathizes with mathematicians, but says OpenAI’s math onslaught won’t stop
slides: Sam Altman acknowledges mathematicians' anxiety — and won't stop anyway
AI models are closing in on formal math proofs
But the bottleneck isn't computation — it's taste
Proof assistants will reshape how researchers verify work
If machines out-prove you, what's your real edge?
thread_text:
1. Your Proof Is Obsolete

Sam Altman says mathematicians are anxious about AI, and he has no plans to slow down. That anxiety is justified: AI models are already closing in on formal proofs.

2. Computation Isn't the Wall

The real bottleneck is taste — knowing which theorems are worth proving. AI can grind through logic, but it can't yet pick the elegant path.

3. Proof Assistants Change Everything

Tools like Lean will soon let researchers verify work in hours, not months. The shift isn't about speed — it's about what becomes possible when checking is cheap.

4. Out-Proven by a Machine?

If AI can out-prove you, your edge isn't raw logic. It's asking the right question before the machine starts computing.

5. Test Your Edge Today

Take a theorem you know and ask an AI to outline a proof. Then ask it why that proof matters. If it can't answer, you've found your real value.
